page: Microsoft Azure D96lds_v7 is an x86_64 compute-optimized server powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz. It features 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, supported by a 480 MB L3 cache. The instance is configured with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 5669 GB NVMe SSD.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in multi-threaded operations and memory bandwidth. The server achieves top-tier results in Passmark CPU tests, including extended instructions, encryption, and physics simulations. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and small-block cached memory read bandwidth also rank in the top tier. For database workloads, the instance demonstrates high efficiency in Redis SET operations and Passmark database operations, alongside strong static web serving throughput.

Due to its compute-oriented design, the D96lds_v7 presents a clear resource tradeoff: it provides massive processing power and high-speed local storage but features a restricted memory footprint of 2.0 GB per vCPU. This makes it highly cost-efficient for CPU-bound workloads that do not require massive RAM arrays, avoiding the premium cost of memory-optimized instances. However, memory-intensive applications may experience bottlenecks.

This server is optimized for high-throughput compute tasks, multi-threaded data processing, and high-performance database operations. It is highly suitable for static web serving, Redis deployments, and CPU-based machine learning tasks such as LLM prompt processing, where its Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions and AVX-512 capabilities can be fully utilized.
description: Microsoft Azure D96lds_v7 is a compute-optimized, x86_64 server designed for high-throughput, CPU-intensive workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz, it delivers 96 vCPUs and 192.0 GB of RAM, representing a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The server includes a 5669 GB local NVMe SSD, providing high-speed storage capacity. Benchmarks show top-tier performance in Passmark CPU tests, multi-threaded decompression, Redis SET operations, and static web serving. It also excels in LLM prompt processing, utilizing Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets. While highly cost-efficient for raw compute and storage-heavy tasks, its low memory-to-core ratio represents a tradeoff for memory-bound applications. It is best suited for high-performance databases, web serving, and parallel data processing.
